question: Holding the V20 anonymous structural state fixed, does Hebrew context-conditioned operator behavior become broadly predictive when consequence recurrence is measured at lemma, lemma-plus-coarse-morphology, or lemma-plus-full-morphology resolution; and specifically, do matched operator/consequence resolutions outperform both one-axis alternatives on sealed holdout and control?
claimBoundary: A positive matched-resolution result supports the claim that V20/V21 used a consequence representation too coarse for the corresponding Hebrew operator representation under this recurrence projector. It does not establish lexical translation, Hebrew-glyph symbol identity, historical contact, common authorship, theology, phonetics, English glosses, or that OSHB morphology is the recovered underlying grammar. Failure of all consequence representations would reject only these recurrence-based consequence definitions, not Hebrew context conditioning itself.

hebrewSource.baseTokenIdentity: first numeric lemma component rendered H<number>
hebrewSource.morphAlignment: exact V21 alignment: split lemma and morph attributes on slash; use the morph segment aligned to the first numeric lemma component; if absent use <MISSING>

fixedStructuralState.state: exact V20/V21 anonymous equality pattern of the previous four BASE LEMMA tokens, padded by <START>; neither operator nor consequence refinement may change the state label
fixedStructuralState.sharedStates: inherit the exact shared-state set frozen by V20; V22 may not reselect states

identityRepresentations.lemmaFullMorph: H<number>|M=<exact V21 aligned OSHB morph segment>

consequenceProjector.rule: use the exact V20 consequence projector, but apply equality/seen/new tests to the frozen identity sequence named by consequenceRepresentation rather than always to base lemma
consequenceProjector.end: END is unchanged because unit boundaries are unchanged
consequenceProjector.baselineCell: operator=lemma, consequence=lemma must reuse the exact inherited V20 Hebrew model and reproduce V20/V21 sealed results before any V22 rescue claim is interpretable

matrix.cells: all 3 operator representations x all 3 consequence representations are frozen before evaluation
matrix.diagnosticCells: the remaining cells are reported to determine whether any gain comes from consequence resolution alone, operator resolution alone, or their compatibility

training.eligibility: TRAIN only, independently within each nonbaseline matrix cell; rank by train frequency then identity under the frozen cap

models.contextOnly: V20-style P0(y|S) learned within each consequence representation from TRAIN
models.invariantOperator: V20-style Pinv(y|S,o): cell-specific state baseline multiplied by the TRAIN-smoothed operator-wide outcome ratio and renormalized
models.contextConditionedOperator: V20-style Pctx(y|S,o) learned from TRAIN (S,o) outcome counts and hierarchically smoothed toward cell Pinv; low-support pairs collapse exactly to Pinv
models.primaryContrast: log2 Pctx(observed y|S,o) - log2 Pinv(observed y|S,o)
models.null: within each cell and operator, permute frozen TRAIN interaction-residual blocks across inherited V20 structural states while leaving the occurrence's Pinv fixed; preserves operator identity, state baseline, residual magnitudes, support pattern, consequence alphabet, and consequence resolution while breaking operator-by-context alignment

pairedAxisComparisons.consequenceAxis: for a primary diagonal cell (r,r), compare its realized context gain against cell (r,lemma) on the same evaluation occurrences and matched operator identities; asks whether changing consequence resolution helps while operator resolution is fixed
pairedAxisComparisons.operatorAxis: for a primary diagonal cell (r,r), compare its realized context gain against cell (lemma,r) on occurrences whose base lemma and refined operator are both evaluable; aggregate occurrence differences within refined operator first; asks whether changing operator resolution helps while consequence resolution is fixed

evaluation.primaryRescueRule: A matched morphology resolution r rescues the recurrence consequence model only if diagonal cell (r,r) passes the within-cell gate in BOTH holdout and control, its consequence-axis advantage over (r,lemma) passes in BOTH lanes, and its operator-axis advantage over (lemma,r) passes in BOTH lanes. No off-diagonal cell can establish a matched-resolution rescue.
evaluation.baselineReproductionRule: the inherited (lemma,lemma) V20 model must reproduce the frozen V20/V21 lane metrics within numerical tolerance 1e-12; otherwise adjudicate IMPLEMENTATION_DRIFT and do not interpret V22

contextProfile.status: secondary only after a primary matched cell rescues
contextProfile.definition: for each inherited V20 shared state, average realized Pctx-vs-Pinv gain within operator first and then across evaluable operators having events in that state
contextProfile.similarity: Pearson correlation of the rescued Hebrew diagonal-cell state-gain profile with the inherited V20 glyph state-gain profile over identical anonymous structural states
contextProfile.null: exactly permute glyph state-profile labels relative to Hebrew when feasible; otherwise 4096 deterministic permutations
